proposedActions: Propose a first comparison using production-representative painted crossmember-to-stringer specimens. AutomVoj would supply fabrication details, specimens and service measurements; Erić would lead fracture examination and testing, subject to agreement. After non-destructive documentation of both failed sections, establish independent levels for thermal cycling (steady chilled versus measured excursions), condensation (dry versus controlled wetting) and vibration (absent versus measured spectrum), holding static belt load, weld condition and coating comparable. Test all eight combinations: baseline, each factor alone, all pairs and the full combination, plus the room-temperature workshop reference. Use separate tuning and held-out evaluation specimens, checking independence. Measure cycles to a predefined detectable crack, crack growth, origin and fracture morphology. Propose two weeks for evidence review and instrumentation planning, followed by a six-week testing window after equipment access is secured, with duration renegotiated against measured service cycles. Reserve scarce failed material through an agreed sampling map. Confirm rig capacity, independent moisture control, safe operation and company engineering allocation before specimen manufacture.

If reproduction passes, use the supported mechanism and a calibrated structural model to select welding, filler or geometry changes on tuning specimens. Compare the best configuration on independent representative specimens under the reproduced exposure, against unchanged production joints. Agree adoption criteria and applicable welding requirements before testing; reduced warranty replacements would remain a longer-term field-validation question.

content.markdown:
# Explaining chilled-store conveyor weld cracking

## Verified facts
- AutomVoj reports cracking after about 18 months at main crossmember-to-stringer connections in painted mild-steel hollow-section frames. Room-temperature loaded workshop tests have not reproduced the failure. [F1]
- The company describes cold-store operation at 2–6 °C and suspects interacting thermal cycling, condensation and loaded-belt vibration; it has not established their causal roles. [F2]
- AutomVoj has site photographs and crack measurements, but only two retained failed sections. [F3]
- AutomVoj lacks low-temperature cyclic-load testing equipment and know-how. Erić’s chamber and servo-hydraulic machine are shared facilities with advance scheduling arrangements. [F4]
- The company has no dedicated R&D department; its chief engineer and two senior automation engineers divide their time between live projects and improvement work. [F5]
- Erić’s published work compared mechanical fatigue with thermal cycling in butt-welded S275JR plates, using excursions between −30 °C and +20 °C. It reported faster crack growth than simple mechanical-plus-thermal predictions, suggesting interaction rather than simple addition. [F6]
- Erić lists openness to joint projects involving low-temperature or combined-loading fatigue testing. [F7]

## Potential benefits
- For the company: The first comparison could distinguish individual and interacting service factors and establish a defensible basis for changing the joint rather than relying on room-temperature tests alone.
- For the researcher: Subject to agreement and access, Erić could test the transfer of thermo-mechanical fatigue methods to coated hollow-section conveyor joints using service measurements, failed-section evidence and controlled comparisons.

## Our inference
- This suggests a relevant joint project, conditional on Erić’s unknown availability and AutomVoj’s agreement. Openness to this format does not establish a commitment or equipment booking.
- Transfer remains unvalidated: colder plate tests do not establish the mechanism in painted hollow-section joints at 2–6 °C. Condensation control and corrosion expertise may require additional support; accelerated loading could also produce an irrelevant fracture mechanism.

## Proposed next steps
- Propose a first comparison using production-representative painted crossmember-to-stringer specimens. AutomVoj would supply fabrication details, specimens and service measurements; Erić would lead fracture examination and testing, subject to agreement. After non-destructive documentation of both failed sections, establish independent levels for thermal cycling (steady chilled versus measured excursions), condensation (dry versus controlled wetting) and vibration (absent versus measured spectrum), holding static belt load, weld condition and coating comparable. Test all eight combinations: baseline, each factor alone, all pairs and the full combination, plus the room-temperature workshop reference. Use separate tuning and held-out evaluation specimens, checking independence. Measure cycles to a predefined detectable crack, crack growth, origin and fracture morphology. Proposed go/no-go: reproduce the observed connection location and fracture features in at least two of three evaluation replicates of the best-supported condition, with measured exposures reproduced and uncertainty reported. Otherwise continue investigation; an inactive single factor does not exclude interactions. No accelerated result establishes an 18-month service life.
- Propose two weeks for evidence review and instrumentation planning, followed by a six-week testing window after equipment access is secured, with duration renegotiated against measured service cycles. Reserve scarce failed material through an agreed sampling map. Confirm rig capacity, independent moisture control, safe operation and company engineering allocation before specimen manufacture.
- If reproduction passes, use the supported mechanism and a calibrated structural model to select welding, filler or geometry changes on tuning specimens. Compare the best configuration on independent representative specimens under the reproduced exposure, against unchanged production joints. Agree adoption criteria and applicable welding requirements before testing; reduced warranty replacements would remain a longer-term field-validation question.

## Open questions
- Can Erić confirm availability and bookable facilities, and can AutomVoj confirm participation in this joint-project format?
- What budget, decision deadline and engineering time can AutomVoj allocate?
- Can AutomVoj authorise examination and limited destructive sampling of the retained sections, provide fabrication and coating records, and arrange representative service-load, temperature and humidity measurements?
- What evidence and applicable design or welding requirements must a proposed modification satisfy before adoption?
